text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Future sporting and cultural events in Vietnam will no longer be sponsored by foreign tobacco and alcohol firms, the prime minister has announced.
- An Asia-Pacific conference for solidarity with Cuba has slammed the U.S. Helms Burton act as "wicked".
- Ho Chi Minh City's Fatherland Front has approved an official list of 32 candidates for next month's National Assembly elections.
- The Standing Committee of the Ho Chi Minh City Party Unit has announced punitive measures for three units and seven officials involved in the Tamexco corruption scandal.
- Provinces throughout Vietnam are opening their third round of discussions to finalise lists of candidates for the National Assembly elections.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong has been awarded a friendship medal by the Russian government for this contribution towards strengthening relations between Hanoi and Moscow.
- Eleven foreign investment projects in Hanoi worth more than $356 million were licensed in the first five months of this year.
- The government will reinforce anti-smuggling units to protect domestic production.
- Vietnam and Israel have signed a memorandum on telecommunications cooperation.
